comment: P1 is wrong for GNU Radio 3.10.12 in the question's scenario. P1 says generating gives default.py if the ID is left at its default, and tutorial.py only if the ID is set to tutorial. But GRC 3.10.12's Save As (also used for the first Save of a new flowgraph) sets the Options ID to the file name when the ID is still 'default'. Saving as tutorial.grc therefore makes the ID tutorial, and generating writes tutorial.py next to the .grc file. The rubric follows an older wiki tutorial. As written, P1 credits the wrong file name and may deny credit to the right one. P2 and P3 are right.
evidence: $ wsl.exe -- bash review_work/scratch/a28/h1b/run8.sh => grc/gui/Application.py 688-694: elif action == Actions.FLOW_GRAPH_SAVE_AS: ... if flow_graph.options_block.params['id'].get_value() == Constants.DEFAULT_FLOW_GRAPH_ID: file_name = os.path.basename(file_path).replace(".grc", ""); flow_graph.options_block.params['id'].set_value(file_name)
$ wsl.exe -- bash review_work/scratch/a28/h1b/run8.sh => grc/core/Constants.py:22: DEFAULT_FLOW_GRAPH_ID = 'default'

$ wsl.exe -- bash review_work/scratch/a28/h1b/run10.sh => Application.py 675-678: elif action == Actions.FLOW_GRAPH_SAVE: # read-only or undefined file path, do save-as ... Actions.FLOW_GRAPH_SAVE_AS()
grc-bench/items/tier_k/dev/rubrics.jsonl :: "default.py if the ID is left at its default, tutorial.py only if the ID is set to tutorial"
suggested_fix: Rewrite P1: 'States that generating writes a Python file named after the Options block's ID (ID + .py) in the same directory as the .grc file; when a flowgraph whose ID is still default is saved as tutorial.grc, GRC sets the ID to tutorial, so the file is tutorial.py (a flowgraph with another ID gives <ID>.py).' Keep P2 and P3.

comment: The points are right: the High Pass Filter block with firdes.high_pass taps and a low cutoff removes DC, the type must match the signal, and a low cutoff needs many taps. But P1 accepts only the High Pass Filter block. GNU Radio's DC Blocker block (filter.dc_blocker_cc/ff, Complex or Float) is a high-pass filter made for exactly this job, and the rubric names it only as an optional extra in P3. An answer built on the DC Blocker would lose P1 although it is a correct, idiomatic answer.
evidence: $ wsl.exe -- bash review_work/scratch/a28/h1b/run7.sh => filter_dc_blocker_xx.block.yml: label: DC Blocker; options: [cc, ff]; option_labels: [Complex->Complex, Float->Float]; make: filter.dc_blocker_${type}(${length}, ${long_form})
